title: Surge Sculptor: tenant-aware burst load generator and customer acceptance protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a deterministically reproducible, tenant-aware burst load generator (code-name: Surge Sculptor) and an associated benchmarking methodology and customer acceptance protocol to validate Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and autoscaler behavior under realistic multi-tenant spikes.
context: Customers often validate our Dedicated SLAs by driving their production-like burst profiles. Existing synthetic probes are single-tenant and fail to capture cross-tenant resource contention, autoscaler hysteresis, and prefix/KV cache warmup effects. This ticket defines the harness, metrics, and pass/fail criteria for an engineering-grade tester that can be used internally by SRE/Performance and externally for customer acceptance runs.
success_criteria: Reproducible harness runs with seed-based scenarios (same seed -> <=3% variance in measured median throughput across runs)
Customer acceptance checklist executed end-to-end including tenant-mix replay and KV-cache priming
Throughput within committed SLA: sustained throughput >= 95% of committed capacity for hold windows defined in profile
Autoscaler behavior: scaling decision latency <= 90s for configured burst profiles and recovery within configured cooldown
Error rate (5xx + throttles) <= 0.1% across sustained and burst phases
Tail latency: p99 <= published threshold for the customer profile during steady-state and burst windows
Fairness metric: no single synthetic tenant consumes >40% of shared resources in multi-tenant scenarios unless explicitly configured
benchmark_architecture: Surge Sculptor is composed of (1) a traffic orchestrator (Golang service) that schedules tenant mixes and dynamic QPS ramps, (2) a replay engine that can read customer traces or synthetic distributions, (3) a KV-cache priming module to seed model caches before measurement, and (4) a telemetry aggregator that collects token-level latencies, RPC metrics, GPU utilization, and autoscaler events. Tests run from an isolated test VPC using dedicated agents and can be sharded across k8s workers.
test_plan: Prepare tenant mixes: small, medium, and enterprise profiles (ratio and prompt length distributions in docs)
Prime KV caches by replaying warmup prefixes for 10 minutes before each measurement window
Execute three phases per run: ramp (5m), sustain (10m), burst (configurable 30-120s spikes), cool-down (10m)
Capture telemetry: request/response timestamps, model variant used, kernel selection logs, batch sizes, queue depth, CPU/GPU metrics, autoscaler decisions and events
Repeat each scenario with 5 different seeds and compute median/variance for each metric
Run cross-tenant fairness runs that include a noisy-neighbor tenant at 30–60% of QPS to validate isolation and throttling behavior
Produce a final acceptance report with pass/fail, traces, aggregated histograms, and artifacts linked to PR/Run IDs
metrics_and_definitions: Sustained Throughput: tokens/sec averaged over sustain window
Peak Burst Throughput: max tokens/sec during burst window
Tail Latency: p95 and p99 token generation latency as measured at API response boundaries
Error Rate: fraction of requests with 5xx or backend-throttle response
Autoscale Latency: time from burst onset to scaled capacity availability (seconds)
Fairness Index: normalized share of GPU cycles per tenant during sustained periods
acceptance_protocol: Customer acceptance runs must be reproducible: a signed scenario YAML (seed, tenant proportions, sequence length distribution, KV priming steps) is provided to customer and executed jointly with an engineering observer. Acceptance passes when all success_criteria items are green, artifacts (telemetry, pcap-like request logs, and run IDs) are uploaded to the customer folder, and an onboarding ticket is created linking the run to their contract.
implementation_notes: Generator service will be implemented in Go for low GC jitter and native concurrency; replay engine will support both protobuf traces and synthetic distributions
Use k8s Jobs with nodeAffinity to pin agent pods to isolated test hardware
Telemetry ingestion via existing metrics pipeline (prometheus + trace-backend); extend exporter to include 'autoscaler.event' with structured tags
Deterministic seeds are critical to reduce run-to-run noise; randomization only for optional exploratory runs
Provide an 'interactive mode' for SRE to step through priming and ramp phases when performing customer-facing runs
decisions: Language: Go selected for generator (concurrency and telemetry maturity)
Warmup duration: default 10 minutes before each sustain window to account for KV cache and kernel JIT
Default burst profiles: short (30s), medium (60s), long (120s) to match customer SLAs
risks: Cluster scheduling variability can add noise > measured deltas; mitigated by running on isolated test nodes
Autoscaler non-determinism under low-util signals may make reaction time noisy; we will instrument and correlate with controller logs
Customer data cannot be used in public harness runs; ensure PII-free traces and signed customer consent for replayed traces
blockers: Dependency on ENG-51001 for provisioning test dedicated nodes
Need security signoff for trace replay (SRE/Security) - see security_review_required
Observability schema change PR must merge (perf-harness#482) before final runs
